newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mostly lower on positioning.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mostly lower on positioning.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed mostly lower on position squaring with nearby September hit by a slide in the cash basis market, traders said.
There was little new feature with U.S. Midwest weather getting mixed reviews as a market factor Friday.
"It was light volume and we'll watch the weather next week for direction," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

At midday, Weather Services Corp noted scattered to widely scattered showers for parts of western Iowa and eastern Nebraska over the weekend while the rest of trhe corn/soy belt was expected to be warm and dry.
"The market is thin and two-sided," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
CBOT grain and soy futures markets will be closed Monday in observance of the U.S. Labor Day holiday.

Late local short covering limited losses and traders said the delivery market had little impact on futures. Friday was first notice day for deliveries on the September and only 40,000 bushels were posted, within the range of estimates.
Soybean futures closed 4-3/4 cents per bushel lower to 1-3/4 higher, with September down 4-3/4 at $8.14-1/2.
Estimated soybean futures volume was at 42,500 contracts, up from 37,030 Thursday.

In the soybean options pit, Continental Grain bought 200 January $8.00 calls and sold 200 January $10.00 calls at 36 cents, traders said, while Ferguson Grain bought 300 March $8.00 calls and sold 300 November $8.00 calls at 22 cents.
Options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, down from 12,984 Thursday.
